Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline has the records needed to pay every affected member directly, so any settlement should use automatic distribution rather than a claims process. We propose a $40 million class fund and $8 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Any reduction in the approved fee would benefit the class, not revert to Brightline. We are open to discussing the amounts while preserving those distribution and reversion protections.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that identified members should be paid automatically, without a claims process, and that any fee reduction should benefit the class. Your proposal totals $48 million, which exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in settlement authority. We offer a $30 million class fund plus up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing agreement. We are open to discussing the allocation within the overall limit.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement on automatic payments and directing any fee reduction to the class. Given the $64 million in disputed charges and the ability to pay members directly, we propose using your stated $40 million overall limit to provide a $34 million class fund and up to $6 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. We would not seek a clear-sailing provision.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree on automatic distribution, no clear-sailing provision, and directing any fee reduction to the class. To resolve the case now while keeping the total outlay below the full authorized limit, we propose a $32 million class fund and up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, for a $38 million maximum outlay.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the agreement on automatic payments, no clear-sailing provision, and directing any fee reduction to class members. To bridge the remaining gap, we propose a $33 million class fund plus up to $6 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses—a $39 million maximum outlay, still below Brightline’s stated authority.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement. To bridge the remaining $1 million gap, we propose splitting it: a $32.5 million class fund plus up to $6 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Payments would be automatic, we would not agree to clear sailing, and any unawarded fees would go to the class. The maximum outlay would be $38.5 million.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $32.5 million class fund, up to $6 million in separately paid court-approved fees and expenses, automatic payments to identified class members, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees paid to the class rather than reverting to Brightline. We will present these terms to the court for approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial automatic-distribution class recovery and a separately paid fee proportionate to the fund. Avoid a fee reverter and clear-sailing provision, both of which could raise approval concerns. Leave room to negotiate given certification risk and the time to trial.

The $48 million demand exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. An automatic distribution and class-favorable treatment of any fee reduction support court approval. Open at $36 million total while leaving room to negotiate.

The $30 million automatic class fund is credible given the $27.5 million trial-value estimate before certification and delay, but Brightline indicates room up to $40 million total. Seek the remaining $4 million for the class while holding fees at $6 million, subject to court approval. Preserve automatic payments and class-directed fee reductions.
The latest proposal has favorable distribution and fee terms but uses the full $40 million authority. Countering at $38 million preserves a meaningful class recovery and room to negotiate.

The defense has confirmed a $40 million ceiling and agreed to automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and class-benefiting fee reductions. A $32 million class fund is substantial, but there is room to seek a better class recovery without jeopardizing the core protections. Counter at $33 million plus up to $6 million in court-approved fees, leaving $1 million below its stated ceiling.
The parties are close, and the proposed structure supports court approval. A $38.5 million midpoint preserves a modest saving while offering a credible path to agreement within the remaining rounds.

The $32.5 million automatic class fund exceeds the $27.5 million probability-weighted trial award before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The $6 million fee remains subject to court approval, any reduction benefits the class, and there is no clear sailing. A further $500,000 counteroffer is not worth risking this strong resolution.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this declaration in support of preliminary approval. Counsel negotiated over three rounds before Hargrove Lane LLP accepted Brightline’s final offer in round four. Our opening proposal included both a $40 million class fund and $8 million in separately paid fees and expenses. Thus, fees were discussed from the outset, not only after class relief was agreed. Brightline initially offered a $30 million class fund and up to $6 million in fees; subsequent exchanges increased the class fund to $32.5 million while retaining a $6 million cap on separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Throughout the negotiations, both sides agreed that identified class members would be paid automatically, without filing claims, and that any fees the court declines to award would go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. Brightline did not agree to refrain from opposing the fee request. The complete negotiation transcript will be filed with the preliminary-approval motion.
